newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: More of the same seen for Malaysia's economy.
newsitem.headline: More of the same seen for Malaysia's economy.

text.p: The Malaysian economy is likely to achieve more of the same in the medium term, an offical with Malayisa's Institute of Strategic and International Studies (ISIS) said on Friday.
Zainal Aznam Yusuf said the Seventh Malaysia plan 1996-2000 had targetted a growth rate of eight percent per annum.
"That target looks, barring major catastrophes, to be within reach," Zainal said in a speech prepared for delivery at a central banking conference in Singapore.
He said inflation remained under control and there was no threat to political stability.
Although gross domestic product (GDP) growth was slowing this year from the very high 9.6 percent of 1995, Zainal said he expected GDP growth of 8.7 percent for 1996.
He said a slowdown in the electronics industry would have a dampening effect on growth but that domestic-oriented industries had been posting fairly sizeable growth.
"Domestic market-oriented industries grew by 17.3 percent in Q1 1996, higher than 4Q 1995's 14.7 percent," he said.
However, "The current account deficit will be sizeable (for 1996) and looks, for the next few years, to be intractable."
